## Source file: 8.3.3.17 - Process lease accounting entries.docx - Path: `Tower Subprocesses/CAPEX/8.3.3.17 - Process lease accounting entries.docx` - Format: DOCX AstraZeneca Finance Process Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) **Title:** 8.3.3.17 - Process lease accounting entries **Process Tower:** Record to Report **Owner:** R2R Global Process Owners Referenced documents such as supporting materials shall be included in the References section below if required Template Version 2.0 17th August 2022 **TABLE OF CONTENTS** [1. PURPOSE [3](#purpose)](#purpose) [2. AUDIENCE [3](#audience)](#audience) [3. SCOPE [3](#scope)](#scope) [4. PROCEDURE [3](#procedure)](#procedure) [4.1 Process Maps [4](#process-maps)](#process-maps) [4.2 Assumptions and Pre-requisites [4](#assumptions-and-pre-requisites)](#assumptions-and-pre-requisites) [4.3 Frequency [4](#frequency)](#frequency) [4.4 Systems and Access [4](#systems-and-access)](#systems-and-access) [4.5 Controls [4](#controls)](#controls) [4.6 Metrics [4](#metrics)](#metrics) [4.7 Process Detail [4](#process-detail)](#process-detail) [5. RESPONSIBILITIES [3](#responsibilities)](#responsibilities) [5.1 Roles and Teams [4](#roles-and-teams)](#roles-and-teams) [6. GLOSSARY [3](#glossary)](#glossary) [7. REFERENCES [3](#references)](#references) [8. Revision history [3](#revision-history)](#revision-history) [9. Appendices [3](#appendices)](#appendices) # # PURPOSE The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to process lease accounting records and create the necessary outputs required to build journal entries from the CoStar Real Estate Manager system. This includes validating the lease accounting records and exporting the data. In the standard process this data is automatically sent to BlackLine where it is automatically prepared as journal entries before being posted. # AUDIENCE This SOP applies to: - GFS Global Lease Team - GFS Middle Office - Embedded Finance (local, hub) - Alexion Regional Controllership # SCOPE The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded: | | | |----|----| | Business Process | Description | | Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR | # # PROCEDURE ## Process Maps ## Assumptions and Pre-requisites The table below contains a summary of the assumptions and pre-requisites required for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | |----|----| | Assumption / Pre-requisite | Description | | Pre-requisite | All participants in this process have the necessary access and training required in CoStar Real Estate Manager. | | Pre-requisite | The creation & modification process has been completed according to the required timeline. | ## Frequency This is a monthly process, executed as part of the period end close. ## Systems and Access The table below contains a summary of the system(s) and accesses required for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | | |----|----|----| | Physical System Name | User Profile / Access Type Required | Description | | CoStar Real Estate Manager (CoStar) | Administrations Lease Accounting – JE Export | Required to execute the exceptions management process and export journals data. | | AZNextgen | R2R messaging | The standard mechanism to engage with the GFS Global Lease team. | ## Controls The table below contains a summary of the control(s) for the process this operating procedure relates to: | Control type | Control ref | Control summary | SOX/FCF | Control Owner | |----|----|----|:--:|----| | Automated | CPX017-001 | CoStar automatically calculates journals from the underlying lease accounting schedules | FCF | GFS Technology - System Delivery R2R | ## Metrics The table below contains a summary of the metrics / measures for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | | | | |----|----|----|----|----| | Metric Id / Name | Metric Type | Metric Description | Metric Owner | Target Value / Output | | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | ## Process Detail The following step by step instructions explain how to perform the work involved in the process:
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.17.1

Review Lease Alerts page

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

This process starts with 8.3.3.13 Approve and review lease accounting record

In this process, check accounting workflow is filtered by “Prepared” and “Approved” to ensure:

  • Any new leases created have an accounting schedule added that has been reviewed before processing lease accounting monthly entries

  • Any modifications added due to any reason have been reviewed before processing lease accounting monthly entries

In the Accounting module, select “Lease Alerts” to view the lease alerts by severity or another criterion. This view is overall for the entire portfolio you have access to.

If you have access to both the AstraZeneca and Alexion portfolios, use the Portfolio filter at the top of the page to select the relevant portfolio you would like to filter for.

To view lease alerts by individual lease, at the top right page of the Abstract, Accounting, Expenses, and/or Revenue pages for that lease, an alerts button will display with the number of alerts in parentheses and the text displaying in accordance with the colour of the most severe alert.

Click the button to display the Lease Alerts pop-up window to process the alerts. After closing out, navigate back to the Lease Alerts page using the breadcrumb trail at the top left of the page.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.17.2

Remediate Alerts
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

In this process, check the type of Lease Alerts. System errors are the result of potential system processing issues. Data audits relate to data input issues.

The team can take one of two actions to investigate and resolve the alert:

  • If the alert requires a change to the lease accounting record, proceed to Task # 8.3.3.17.6 Request change from in-country finance team.

  • If a lease alert does not give any potential financial impact, proceed to Task # 8.3.3.17.3 Dismiss alert with valid reason.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.17.3

Dismiss lease alerts with valid reason
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

Click the Dismiss button and select a reason for dismissal. Once processed a confirmation message will be displayed.

One can also select the ‘Enter Custom Reason’ option to enter a free text reason for the dismissal, and then click ‘Dismiss’.

Note: This task cannot be done on leases that are locked for batch accounting.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.17.4

Journal Entry to approve
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

This step is performed when two validations are completed

In the Accounting module, select ‘Journal Entries to Approve’.

On the Journal Entry Approval screen, select the filters desired to narrow down the search results but all others are optional.

  • Portfolio – AstraZeneca / Alexion.

  • Country - Select country as required.

  • Period - Current month when performed.

  • Workflow status - All workflow status should be reviewed prior to approving journal entries.

  • Classification type: IFRS 16.

  • Journal Entry Profile: Use the dropdown to select the relevant profiles, depending on whether the lease you are approving should be directed towards the SAP S/4HANA or ECC(Blackline) journal entry processing. Following this, data is ingested by BlackLine and transformed into SAP journal entries using the Automated Journal Definition (AJD) functionality, according to specific logic developed in the BlackLine Journal Entry module. # AUDIENCE This SOP applies to the below audience: - GFS Global Lease Team - GFS Business Administration # SCOPE The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.18.1

Transmit lease accounting entries

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

The intent of this step is to capture all the data required to carry out IFRS 16 compliant accounting within the CoStar system

This process starts from Task# 8.3.3.17: 4.7.1 Process lease accounting entries.

Reversing Journal Entry Status (Un-export & Un-approve)

When the journal entry for a lease has been approved and exported within CoStar, the JE Status column in the accounting schedule will change from Scheduled to Approved to Exported.

Once the status is marked as ‘Exported’, the lease will no longer appear in the Journal Entry to Approve or Journal Entry to Export, or AstraZeneca/Alexion JE Export reports to prevent re-processing of the journal entry. In the event if the user needs to modify an accounting schedule after journal entries have been exported, they will need to go through the following steps to revert the JE Status back to ‘Scheduled’. The user can make modifications for a period when it’s in ‘Scheduled’ status, then will go through the Journal Entries to Approve and Journal Entries to Export steps again for this lease.

1) Navigate to the lease record by using the quick search or list pages in the Portfolio module.

2) Navigate to the Accounting page.

3) On the accounting schedule, locate the JE Status for the period that needs to be reversed. Click ‘Exported’.

4) In the pop up, review the journal entry that has been exported. Select ‘unexport’.

5) After the system has unexported the journal, select unapprove.

6) The pop up should now display Preview Journal Entry. Select ‘Close’.

7) Ensure the JE Status for the period is now marked as Scheduled before making any changes to the lease record.

Changes can be made to expenses, allocations or other information that should have been updated before processing the journal entry. Navigate to Journal Entries to Approve,Journal Entries to Export, or AstraZeneca/Alexion JE Export reports to reprocess the journal entry for the period. If more than one lease should be reversed, follow the steps for Offline Reversal for Journal Entry.

Offline Reversals for Journal Entries

Journal entry reversal occurs via an offline report located in the Reports module. The report is called Offline Reverse Journal Entry. Journal entries follow a 2-step process of approval and export, and both the unexport and unapprove can be accommodated in the Offline Reverse Journal Entry report.

1) Navigate to the Reports module.

2) Search for ‘Offline reverse’.

3) Select Offline Reverse Journal Entry report.

4) Complete the criteria listed below as needed to filter the file for the appropriate journal entries that need to be reversed.

• Hierarchy

• Period From

• Period To

• Classification Type

• Amortization Profile

• Journal Entry Profile

• Journal Entry Status*

• Currency

• Workflow Status

• Country

• System Export Batch ID

• Client Batch Number

*Note - The filter for Journal Entry Status has the biggest impact on the content of the report. One must select either Approved or Exported as the status.

5) Based the selection of filters, the system will generate an Excel file to complete.

6) Open the Excel file and find the Actions column. Available Actions in the report for each journal entry will vary as follows:

• If Journal Entry Status was Approved – Actions: unapprove, Skip

• If Journal Entry Status was Exported – Actions: unexport, unexport & unapprove, Skip

7) Review each row and make an update to the Action column, indicating what action to take for each lease.

8) Save the Excel file.

9) Navigate to the Reports module.

10) Upload the Excel file by clicking the Upload Offline Template and following the prompts. It may take up to 15 minutes to complete the processing once the file has been uploaded.

Note: In the event unexport/unapproved action is performed in CoStar, a reversal journal should be manually prepared to post in Blackline. This process should undergo the normal journal posting in Blackline as per Blackline policy.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.18.2

Build lease accounting journals
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Business Administrator GFS Business Administrator N/A N/A

Once the sFTP file is transmitted to the lease accounting journal, it will send to the Blackline tool via global scape for producing of the JE template.

After it has been sent to the Blackline tool, the Lease accounting journal is prepared in the BL template and Blackline admin will process the automated journal entry on WD-1, It leads to follow two processes as per scenarios.

  • If all fields in the template are correctly validated in Blackline and there are no errors, the posting has been successfully completed. Follow task 8.3.2.24. Process Automated Journal Entries where the impact will be documented in the SAP lease accounting books.

  • If any errors are encountered (E.g. Cost Centre is blocked, Internal Order does not exist etc., the workflow will automatically be assigned to a member of the Global Lease team for manual remediation. Once updated detail is received and updated in the BL template the manual JE can be processed with the impact shown in the Lease account in SAP books.

  1. Status will remain as Not Prepared

  1. Entry will be required to be updated to resolve the errors and select Validate and Certify.

  • Once the month end lease entry is posted in SAP, this process is completed.

steps.title: Transmit lease accounting entries
steps.detail:
The intent of this step is to capture all the data required to carry out IFRS 16 compliant accounting within the CoStar system

This process starts from Task# 8.3.3.17: 4.7.1 Process lease accounting entries.

Reversing Journal Entry Status (Un-export & Un-approve)

When the journal entry for a lease has been approved and exported within CoStar, the JE Status column in the accounting schedule will change from Scheduled to Approved to Exported.

Once the status is marked as ‘Exported’, the lease will no longer appear in the Journal Entry to Approve or Journal Entry to Export, or AstraZeneca/Alexion JE Export reports to prevent re-processing of the journal entry. In the event if the user needs to modify an accounting schedule after journal entries have been exported, they will need to go through the following steps to revert the JE Status back to ‘Scheduled’. The user can make modifications for a period when it’s in ‘Scheduled’ status, then will go through the Journal Entries to Approve and Journal Entries to Export steps again for this lease.

1) Navigate to the lease record by using the quick search or list pages in the Portfolio module.

2) Navigate to the Accounting page.

3) On the accounting schedule, locate the JE Status for the period that needs to be reversed. Click ‘Exported’.

4) In the pop up, review the journal entry that has been exported. Select ‘unexport’.

5) After the system has unexported the journal, select unapprove.

6) The pop up should now display Preview Journal Entry. Select ‘Close’.

7) Ensure the JE Status for the period is now marked as Scheduled before making any changes to the lease record.

Changes can be made to expenses, allocations or other information that should have been updated before processing the journal entry. Navigate to Journal Entries to Approve,Journal Entries to Export, or AstraZeneca/Alexion JE Export reports to reprocess the journal entry for the period. If more than one lease should be reversed, follow the steps for Offline Reversal for Journal Entry.

Offline Reversals for Journal Entries

Journal entry reversal occurs via an offline report located in the Reports module. The report is called Offline Reverse Journal Entry. Journal entries follow a 2-step process of approval and export, and both the unexport and unapprove can be accommodated in the Offline Reverse Journal Entry report.

1) Navigate to the Reports module.

2) Search for ‘Offline reverse’.

3) Select Offline Reverse Journal Entry report.

4) Complete the criteria listed below as needed to filter the file for the appropriate journal entries that need to be reversed.

Hierarchy

Period From

Period To

Classification Type

Amortization Profile

Journal Entry Profile

Journal Entry Status*

Currency

Workflow Status

Country

System Export Batch ID

Client Batch Number

*Note - The filter for Journal Entry Status has the biggest impact on the content of the report. One must select either Approved or Exported as the status.

5) Based the selection of filters, the system will generate an Excel file to complete.

6) Open the Excel file and find the Actions column. Available Actions in the report for each journal entry will vary as follows:

If Journal Entry Status was Approved - Actions: unapprove, Skip

If Journal Entry Status was Exported - Actions: unexport, unexport & unapprove, Skip

7) Review each row and make an update to the Action column, indicating what action to take for each lease.

8) Save the Excel file.

9) Navigate to the Reports module.

10) Upload the Excel file by clicking the Upload Offline Template and following the prompts. It may take up to 15 minutes to complete the processing once the file has been uploaded.

Note: In the event unexport/unapproved action is performed in CoStar, a reversal journal should be manually prepared to post in Blackline. This process should undergo the normal journal posting in Blackline as per Blackline policy.

steps.title: Build lease accounting journals
steps.detail:
Once the sFTP file is transmitted to the lease accounting journal, it will send to the Blackline tool via global scape for producing of the JE template.

After it has been sent to the Blackline tool, the Lease accounting journal is prepared in the BL template and Blackline admin will process the automated journal entry on WD-1, It leads to follow two processes as per scenarios.

If all fields in the template are correctly validated in Blackline and there are no errors, the posting has been successfully completed. Follow task 8.3.2.24. Process Automated Journal Entries where the impact will be documented in the SAP lease accounting books.

If any errors are encountered (E.g. Cost Centre is blocked, Internal Order does not exist etc., the workflow will automatically be assigned to a member of the Global Lease team for manual remediation. Once updated detail is received and updated in the BL template the manual JE can be processed with the impact shown in the Lease account in SAP books.

Status will remain as Not Prepared

Entry will be required to be updated to resolve the errors and select Validate and Certify.

Once the month end lease entry is posted in SAP, this process is completed.

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A N/A

Prior to month end close, an initial depreciation test run is conducted at mid-month to help identify if there are any issues / errors to ensure resolution is in place. Mid-month test run is followed in all regions except NAM as NAM does not have mid-month schedule job run.

  1. Run Depreciation Test Run

Login to SAP.

Input SAP T-code AFAB and press Enter.

Please update the following fields:

  • Company Code

  • Fiscal Year: Current year

  • Posting Period: Current posting period

Tick “List assets”. Make sure that “Test Run” has also been ticked. Click on execute icon to proceed.

  1. Run Depreciation in Foreground and Background

Select between Option 1 or Option 2 to run depreciation:

Option 1: Running depreciation in Foreground if the number of fixed assets is low.
For Option 1, refer to sub-step B.1) Run Depreciation in Foreground and update working file.

Option 2: Running depreciation in Background if the number of fixed assets is high. This option requires another T- code to view the result.
For Option 2, refer to sub-step B.2) Run Depreciation in Background.

B.1) Option 1: Run Depreciation in Foreground and update working file

At the top left of the page, go to “Program”, then select “Execute” (or press F8 which performs the same function).

A pop up “Limitation online” will appear, warning that executing the Depreciation Run is limited to approximately 1000 assets. Click “Yes” to Proceed.

If the Depreciation Test Run is successful with no errors, there will be a statement highlighting “TESTRUN completed successfully” at the end of the page. If there are any errors, proceed to Step 4.7.2: 8.3.3.6.2 Investigate errors. The errors could be due to Cost Centres or Internal Orders being blocked.

Export the file to excel: Click on the Export to local file button (Or press F9).

Select the spreadsheet option and click on the green tick highlighted below.

Select the file path where you want to export and name the file, then click Generate. The report will be exported to excel.

Obtain the prior month’s working file of FA Movement and Analysis Template from the shared location. Please refer to Section 9 for the template to be used for FA Movement and analysis.

Save the previous month’s working file as the current month working file.

In the AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis file, copy and replace the data from columns A to P in ‘AFAB last mth’ tab.

Then, go back to ‘AFAB’ tab and clear all data from columns B to P.

Next, open the depreciation posting run report which was previously generated and saved. Finally, copy the data into the cleared table in AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis File. Copy only into Column B to Column P (Grey Headers).

The columns with yellow headers either contain a formula or are for the report preparer’s remarks. The formula in Column A is a concatenation of Column B and Column C.

B.2) Option 2: Run Depreciation in Background

Go to the top left of the page, go to “Program”, then select “Execute in Background” (or press F9).

A pop up “Background Print Parameters” will appear. Enter the Output Device as “local_en”. Click on the green tick to continue.

Another pop up will appear for the user’s information. Click on the green tick to continue.

The next pop up is to indicate when the job should run. In this instance, click on “Immediate” for immediate run, then click on Save (or Ctrl+S).

At the bottom of the page, the message “Background job was scheduled for program RAPOST20000” will appear.

  1. View depreciation job in SAP

To view the depreciation job, from any page in SAP Click on “System” > then select “Own Jobs”

On clicking on own jobs, the screen below will appear:

This is a Finished Job. It will be highlighted in green.

Make sure the Job has the green status: “Finished”. If it is not yet finished, the status will state “Active”. In that case simply keep refreshing the page periodically by clicking on the Refresh button (or “F8”).

If the job is finished, proceed to select the job, then click the Spool button.

Select the button, which will show the Spooled Depreciation Test Run result.

If the Depreciation Test Run is successful with no errors, the following screen will show:

Note: The report will only show the first 10 pages.

If the depreciation test run was unsuccessful, the following screen will be displayed.

Click on log box icon () to view error message and reason of the failed test run.

Generally – there are two reasons for failed test runs:

  • Posting to prior month which has already been posted, as shown in the screen below:

  • Posting to the subsequent month before the current period is posted, as shown in the screen below:

Export the report and save it to a local file by clicking on .

Export the report

The report will be exported.

Open the Excel File, which will appear as below:

Select all the rows. Then go to Data --> Text to Columns as highlighted below:

In the next screen, adjust the field widths according to the columns required in the Depreciation Analysis file by using the lines with arrows as shown below. After that, click “Finish”.

The data is now split as required. The data is now ready to be pasted into the AFAB Tab in the Depreciation Analysis file.

Copy the raw data into the AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis File. The data to be transferred should only be entered Column B to Column P. The formula in Column A is a concatenation of Column B and Column C. Make sure the formula is copied to cover all the asset lines.

Using Column A, the formula in Column Q will use VLOOKUP to “AFAB last month” tab’s Column A and Column N to get last month’s depreciation posted for the same asset.

There will be another test run during month-end after all asset postings have been completed. The test run functionality of ERP is utilised. Any issues or errors encountered will have to be resolved before the depreciation run can be completed in production mode.

Note: Month end depreciation test run for NAM Hubs is performed with an automated background scheduled job on WD-4 (US time 22:00) on monthly basis.

To check the test run result from the scheduled background job, use T-code AFBP to check the posting log of schedule run.

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A N/A

If there are no errors in the depreciation test run, GFS Back Office R2R will perform the analysis of the depreciation test run figures, comparing them with prior month depreciation figures. A review is performed of depreciation expenditure to ensure that the monthly cost is recorded accurately. Ensure you perform control CPX011 as per the FCAS framework for your unit.

Perform Analysis on Depreciation

In the “Dep Analysis” Tab of the FA Movement and Analysis Template, both month’s data (previous month and current month) will be derived from formulas in the table below, which represents the FA Sub ledger.

Last month (Col D): = SUMIF(‘AFAB last month!D:D,’Dep Analysis_RU10’!C110,’AFAB last month’!N:N).

On a review of the current month depreciation against the previous month's depreciation, if variance is above threshold (+/- Threshold) as per the Capital and Fixed Asset Standard (Please refer to the link in Section 9 Appendices), the variance must be further investigated and assessed for reasonableness.

  1. Investigate and explain any variances

  1. Summarise the cause for depreciation variance

In the “Dep Analysis” Tab, there is a summary of the cause of variance which was encountered (illustrative purposes only).

Depreciation variances can be caused by many factors. Below is a list of common causes of depreciation variances:

Common causes of decreased depreciation:

  • Asset Retirements in the last month / current month

  • Assets fully depreciated in the last month

  • There was an unusually large depreciation amount for the last month (e.g. accelerated depreciation following an impairment review), so compared to the current month’s depreciation, it would appear to be low

Common causes of increased depreciation:

  • Asset Acquisitions / AUC Capitalisations in last month / current month

  • Assets with depreciation start dates brought forward / moved to an earlier date (resulting in an increased depreciation in the following months to normalise total depreciation value)

The table below indicates how to check for common causes of depreciation variances:

B.1) Increased Depreciation:

Common Causes How to Check for it Action Step
New Asset Capitalised during the month Go to SAP T-code AS03, and go to the General Tab. Check the field “Capitalised on date” No further action required
Depreciation start date brought forward Go to SAP T-code AS03, and view depreciation start date Verify with market if it was intended to bring forward the date

B.2) Decreased Depreciation:

Common Causes How to Check for it Action Step
Net book value is zero This can be checked by checking asset NBV in SAP T-code AW01N. No further action required
Unusually large depreciation in last month (special cases)

  • Check if last month’s increase was due to changes in the asset’s depreciation start date (using SAP T-code AW01N) through Tab “Posted Value”

  • Check if the large depreciation value was due to change in useful life (Using SAP T-code AS03 through tab “Deprec. Area)

  • Check if last month’s increase was due to changes in the asset’s depreciation start date, caused by backdated depreciation (Using SAP T- code AW01N) through Tab “Parameters” check Ord.dep.start date and make comparison through tab “Comparison”

  • If there was a change in depreciation start date, the legitimacy of the change would have been verified in the previous month; hence no further action required

  • If there was a change in useful life, verify with the market whether this was intended

Depreciation is allocated by cost centre defined in the Asset Master Record. The processer will run depreciation for all active fixed assets on a monthly basis, as per the Global Close Calendar. The depreciation key defines the method that will be used to calculate depreciation for the asset.

Depreciation areas are set up to calculate depreciation for different purposes such as Group book, Local GAAP or Tax depreciation.

The output of the depreciation process will be the depreciation postings in each of the relevant depreciation areas, by the amount calculated as defined by the depreciation key. This will result in an adjustment of the Net Book Value of the Fixed Assets. Note that Group book and Local GAAP depreciation are posted to the General Ledger (GL) at the same time upon running AFAB whilst Tax depreciation is displayed in the AA module for reporting purposes.

steps.title: Execute Initial Depreciation mid-month (Test Run)
steps.detail:
Prior to month end close, an initial depreciation test run is conducted at mid-month to help identify if there are any issues / errors to ensure resolution is in place. Mid-month test run is followed in all regions except NAM as NAM does not have mid-month schedule job run.

Run Depreciation Test Run

Login to SAP.

Input SAP T-code AFAB and press Enter.

Please update the following fields:

Company Code

Fiscal Year: Current year

Posting Period: Current posting period

Tick “List assets”. Make sure that “Test Run” has also been ticked. Click on execute icon to proceed.

Run Depreciation in Foreground and Background

Select between Option 1 or Option 2 to run depreciation:

Option 1: Running depreciation in Foreground if the number of fixed assets is low.

For Option 1, refer to sub-step B.1) Run Depreciation in Foreground and update working file.

Option 2: Running depreciation in Background if the number of fixed assets is high. This option requires another T- code to view the result.

For Option 2, refer to sub-step B.2) Run Depreciation in Background.

B.1) Option 1: Run Depreciation in Foreground and update working file

At the top left of the page, go to “Program”, then select “Execute” (or press F8 which performs the same function).

A pop up “Limitation online” will appear, warning that executing the Depreciation Run is limited to approximately 1000 assets. Click “Yes” to Proceed.

If the Depreciation Test Run is successful with no errors, there will be a statement highlighting “TESTRUN completed successfully” at the end of the page. If there are any errors, proceed to Step 4.7.2: 8.3.3.6.2 Investigate errors. The errors could be due to Cost Centres or Internal Orders being blocked.

Export the file to excel: Click on the Export to local file button  (Or press F9).

Select the spreadsheet option and click on the green tick highlighted below.

Select the file path where you want to export and name the file, then click Generate. The report will be exported to excel.

Obtain the prior month’s working file of FA Movement and Analysis Template from the shared location. Please refer to Section 9 for the template to be used for FA Movement and analysis.

Save the previous month’s working file as the current month working file.

In the AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis file, copy and replace the data from columns A to P in ‘AFAB last mth’ tab.

Then, go back to ‘AFAB’ tab and clear all data from columns B to P.

Next, open the depreciation posting run report which was previously generated and saved. Finally, copy the data into the cleared table in AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis File. Copy only into Column B to Column P (Grey Headers).

The columns with yellow headers either contain a formula or are for the report preparer’s remarks. The formula in Column A is a concatenation of Column B and Column C.

B.2) Option 2: Run Depreciation in Background

Go to the top left of the page, go to “Program”, then select “Execute in Background” (or press F9).

A pop up “Background Print Parameters” will appear. Enter the Output Device as “local_en”. Click on the green tick to continue.

Another pop up will appear for the user’s information. Click on the green tick to continue.

The next pop up is to indicate when the job should run. In this instance, click on “Immediate” for immediate run, then click on Save  (or Ctrl+S).

At the bottom of the page, the message “Background job was scheduled for program RAPOST20000” will appear.

View depreciation job in SAP

To view the depreciation job, from any page in SAP Click on “System” > then select “Own Jobs”

On clicking on own jobs, the screen below will appear:

This is a Finished Job. It will be highlighted in green.

Make sure the Job has the green status: “Finished”. If it is not yet finished, the status will state “Active”. In that case simply keep refreshing the page periodically by clicking on the Refresh button (or “F8”).

If the job is finished, proceed to select the job, then click the Spool button.

Select the button, which will show the Spooled Depreciation Test Run result.

If the Depreciation Test Run is successful with no errors, the following screen will show:

Note: The report will only show the first 10 pages.

If the depreciation test run was unsuccessful, the following screen will be displayed.

Click on log box icon () to view error message and reason of the failed test run.

Generally - there are two reasons for failed test runs:

Posting to prior month which has already been posted, as shown in the screen below:

Posting to the subsequent month before the current period is posted, as shown in the screen below:

To view the full report, click on Settings as highlighted below:

In the pop up, change the Display area to show “From page” 1 to a sufficiently large number of pages to cover the whole report.

The warning below will pop-up as shown. Click on the green tick or press Enter.

Export the report and save it to a local file by clicking on .

Export the report

Select Text with Tabs and click on the green tick .

Select where the file is to be exported to and name the file, then click Generate.

The report will be exported.

Open the Excel File, which will appear as below:

Select all the rows. Then go to Data --> Text to Columns as highlighted below:

In the pop up, select “Fixed width” and click “Next”.

In the next screen, adjust the field widths according to the columns required in the Depreciation Analysis file by using the lines with arrows as shown below. After that, click “Finish”.

The data is now split as required. The data is now ready to be pasted into the AFAB Tab in the Depreciation Analysis file.

Copy the raw data into the AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis File. The data to be transferred should only be entered Column B to Column P. The formula in Column A is a concatenation of Column B and Column C. Make sure the formula is copied to cover all the asset lines.

Using Column A, the formula in Column Q will use VLOOKUP to “AFAB last month” tab’s Column A and Column N to get last month’s depreciation posted for the same asset.

The formula in Column R is the difference between Column N (amount to be posted) and Column Q (amount posted in previous month).

Go to column “H” in tab “Dep Analysis_RU10” and look at the variances.

Note: If the variance is more than USD 1m by account determination in “AFAB” tab or more than 5% in “Dep Analysis” tab column G, the processer needs to explain the reason of movement (i.e. sales of asset, etc.) in column S in “AFAB” tab.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Investigate error
steps.detail:
GFS Back Office R2R needs to investigate errors in the depreciation run and liaise with the relevant teams, depending on the error's nature.

Identify nature of error

While running the depreciation through the system, the user may encounter errors due to:

Technical Issues encountered in SAP

Other common issues (e.g. cost centre closed, insufficient master data entered)

Escalate error

Once the root cause is determined, reach out to relevant parties who can assist with error resolution:

Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office for other common issues (Proceed to Step 4.7.3: 8.3.3.6.3 Assist with Issue resolution)

IT for technical issues (Proceed to Step 4.7.7: 8.3.3.6.7 Contact IT Help Desk and Raise Ticket)

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Assist with Error Resolution
steps.detail:
Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office will need to assist to resolve the issue. Generally, errors are due to Cost Centres or Internal Orders that were closed and need to be reopened for depreciation.

Assist with error resolution

For common errors relating to blocked Cost Centres, check if the cost centre should be unblocked, or whether the asset should be transferred to a different cost centre. In both cases, contact GFS Back Office DMT which performs cost centre updates.

Confirm if mid-month was run, and respond to GFS Back Office R2R

Once the error is resolved, revert to GFS Back Office R2R accordingly, who will proceed with options below (Please note this is not applicable for NAM as NAM does not follow mid-month schedule job run):

If mid-month test was conducted, proceed to Step 4.7.6: 8.3.3.6.6 Execute depreciation at month end (Test run).

If mid-month test was not yet conducted, proceed to Step 4.7.4: 8.3.3.6.4 All Asset Postings received (pre-month-end).

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: All Asset Postings received (Pre-month-end)
steps.detail:
All fixed asset posting requests needs to be sent to GFS Back Office R2R as part of the pre-closing activities.

Obtain all asset postings: Markets to request asset transactions on or before the deadline as per the Global Close Calendar Standard. All postings received by the request deadline will need to be processed by the Back Office, prior to the asset posting deadline as per GCC. This covers requests for asset acquisition, scrapping, retirement, sale, impairment etc.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Complete all asset postings
steps.detail:
Perform all Fixed Asset Postings

All postings received by the requested deadline will need to be processed by the Back Office, prior to the asset posting deadline as per GCC.

This ensures that:

There are no pending requests to change Fixed Asset Cost Centres

All assets to be retired in that month and with the depreciation policy not to depreciate in the month of disposal have been processed before the Depreciation run

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Execute Depreciation at month end (test run)
steps.detail:
There will be another test run during month-end after all asset postings have been completed. The test run functionality of ERP is utilised. Any issues or errors encountered will have to be resolved before the depreciation run can be completed in production mode.

Note: Month end depreciation test run for NAM Hubs is performed with an automated background scheduled job on WD-4 (US time 22:00) on monthly basis.

To check the test run result from the scheduled background job, use T-code AFBP to check the posting log of schedule run.

At parameter in the below SAP screen, input Company Code, Fiscal Year and Posting Period. Tick on “SchedMan Monitor” - Schedule Manager: Monitor then click on execute .

Following screen displays all historical job logs. Double click on “ Depreciation posting run” entry and the status will change to “green” status which means posting run is completed without error.

The next panel will appear as below. Click on “Additional Info”, to confirm the company code, and posting period. Click on back icon  to download the list of posting log.

On the next page, uncheck “SchedMan Monitor” and check on “List assets” . Click on execute icon  to proceed.

The result of total depreciation posting will be displayed at the bottom of the report at column “Amount to be posted”. Take a copy of screenshot of the posting run result with time stamp as CPX011 control supporting. This screenshot is used to match the current month’s totals in the Dep Analysis tab in Depreciation variance analysis template. Refer sub-step 8.3.3.6.9 Perform Analysis on Depreciation.

Execute Depreciation Test Run

Execute Depreciation Test run as per month end closing schedule (WD - 2). Test run steps are similar to the mid-month depreciation test performed.

For detailed steps, please refer to Step 4.7.1: 8.3.3.6.1 Execute initial depreciation at mid-month.

If there are errors encountered while executing the test-run, proceed to Step 4.7.2: 8.3.3.6.2 Investigate error, to follow similar error resolution process as performed during mid-month test run.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Contact IT Help Desk & Raise Ticket
steps.detail:
If a technical issue is encountered during the run, GFS Back Office R2R will contact the IT help desk and raise a ticket for the case.

Raise Ticket to IT Help Desk

Go to web link: https://azprod.service-now.com/navpage.do

Raise a ticket according to technical issue faced, along with the relevant descriptions and supporting screenshots.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Resolve Error
steps.detail:
IT supports the case until the technical error is resolved.

Resolve and respond to technical error raised

Support and close technical issue raised.

Once error has been resolved, respond to GFS Back Office R2R through email, who will then confirm if mid-month test run was conducted.

If mid-month test run was not yet conducted, GFS Back Office R2R to proceed with Step 4.7.4: 8.3.3.6.4 All asset postings received (pre-month-end).

If mid-month test run was conducted, GFS Back Office R2R to proceed with Step 4.7.6: 8.3.3.6.6 Execute depreciation at month end (Test run).

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Perform variance analysis against prior month depreciation
steps.detail:
If there are no errors in the depreciation test run, GFS Back Office R2R will perform the analysis of the depreciation test run figures, comparing them with prior month depreciation figures. A review is performed of depreciation expenditure to ensure that the monthly cost is recorded accurately. Ensure you perform control CPX011 as per the FCAS framework for your unit.

Perform Analysis on Depreciation

In the “Dep Analysis” Tab of the FA Movement and Analysis Template, both month’s data (previous month and current month) will be derived from formulas in the table below, which represents the FA Sub ledger.

Last month (Col D): = SUMIF(‘AFAB last month!D:D,’Dep Analysis_RU10’!C110,’AFAB last month’!N:N).

This month (Col E) =SUMIF('AFAB_Current month'!D:D,'Dep Analysis_RU10'!C117,'AFAB_Current month'!N:N)

Column F is the Variance Value, and this is the difference between current month (Col E) and previous month (Col D).

Column G is the variance value in USD.

To determine the USD value of the variance in local currency, go to this link of Azure Lite website and scroll down to identify the budgeted rate for the currency of the market. For e.g. in the above report, the currency RUB is to be converted to USD currency.

Screen will appear as below after selecting below parameters in drop down:

Rate Type: Budget and Forecast rates

Year: Current year

Period: Current month

The Base rate is mentioned in G1 and use the formula in Column G = F110/$G$2:

Column H is the variance value in percentage, dividing Variance Value (Col F) by previous month’s value (Col D).

A screenshot of the successful Depreciation test run (either run in foreground or run in background) will need to be pasted into Depreciation analysis’s “Dep Print Screen” Tab.

Successful depreciation page (Option 1: Running in foreground) is shown below. The numbers here will tie back to the total of column E in ‘Dep Analysis’ tab.

Successful depreciation page (Option 2: Running in background) is shown below.

This is a Finished Job. It will be highlighted in green.

If variance for any fixed asset is above threshold (+/- Threshold) as per AZ Capital and Fixed Assets standard, proceed to Step 4.7.10: 8.3.3.6.10 Investigate Variance.

If variance does not exceed threshold (+/- Threshold), proceed to Step 4.7.14: 8.3.3.6.14: Execute depreciation (production).

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Investigate Variance
steps.detail:
On a review of the current month depreciation against the previous month's depreciation, if variance is above threshold (+/- Threshold) as per the Capital and Fixed Asset Standard (Please refer to the link in Section 9 Appendices), the variance must be further investigated and assessed for reasonableness.

Further reports can be run to double check the results and review for reasonableness (e.g. Asset Report by Class, Addition Report and Disposal / Retirement Report).

If the identified variance does not pass the reasonableness test, proceed to Step 4.7.11: 8.3.3.6.11 Provide assistance with variance explanation.

Investigate and explain any variances

The percentage in Column I will turn red if the variance exceeds the threshold. The data in “AFAB” and “AFAB last mth” tabs will be used to find out which assets are causing the variances, and from there the reason for the variance can be identified.

Summarise the cause for depreciation variance

In the “Dep Analysis” Tab, there is a summary of the cause of variance which was encountered (illustrative purposes only).

Depreciation variances can be caused by many factors. Below is a list of common causes of depreciation variances:

Common causes of decreased depreciation:

Asset Retirements in the last month / current month

Assets fully depreciated in the last month

There was an unusually large depreciation amount for the last month (e.g. accelerated depreciation following an impairment review), so compared to the current month’s depreciation, it would appear to be low

Common causes of increased depreciation:

Asset Acquisitions / AUC Capitalisations in last month / current month

Assets with depreciation start dates brought forward / moved to an earlier date (resulting in an increased depreciation in the following months to normalise total depreciation value)

The table below indicates how to check for common causes of depreciation variances:

B.1) Increased Depreciation:

Common Causes

How to Check for it

Action Step

New Asset Capitalised during the month

Go to SAP T-code AS03, and go to the General Tab. Check the field “Capitalised on date”

No further action required

Depreciation start date brought forward

Go to SAP T-code AS03, and view depreciation start date

Verify with market if it was intended to bring forward the date

B.2) Decreased Depreciation:

Common Causes

How to Check for it

Action Step

Net book value is zero

This can be checked by checking asset NBV in SAP T-code AW01N.

No further action required

Unusually large depreciation in last month (special cases)

Check if last month’s increase was due to changes in the asset’s depreciation start date (using SAP T-code AW01N) through Tab “Posted Value”

Check if the large depreciation value was due to change in useful life (Using SAP T-code AS03 through tab “Deprec. Area)

Check if last month’s increase was due to changes in the asset’s depreciation start date, caused by backdated depreciation (Using SAP T- code AW01N) through Tab “Parameters” check Ord.dep.start date and make comparison through tab “Comparison”

If there was a change in depreciation start date, the legitimacy of the change would have been verified in the previous month; hence no further action required

If there was a change in useful life, verify with the market whether this was intended

Determine reasonableness (+/- Threshold)

For variance which exceeds threshold as identified in the Depreciation Analysis file, double check and review other reports for reasonableness, such as:

Asset Report by class

Addition Report

Disposal / Retirement Report

If asset passes the reasonableness test, proceed to Step 4.7.14: 8.3.3.6.14 Execute depreciation (production).

If asset does not pass reasonableness test, proceed to Step 4.7.11: 8.3.3.6.11 Provide assistance with variance explanation.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Provide assistance with Variance Explanation
steps.detail:
Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office supports GFS Back Office R2R in their analysis of the variance, in case the reasonableness test is not passed. Asset movements at the sites can be reviewed to support any significant differences in the depreciation figures.

Receive and analyse depreciation analysis file

Once depreciation file has been received, review initial variance analysis performed by GFS Back Office R2R.

Provide assistance on variance explanation

Determine if variance (which gets communicated back to GFS Back Office R2R) was due to Fixed Asset Master Data.

If yes, proceed to Step 4.7.12: 8.3.3.6.12 Coordinate to update Fixed Assets Master Data.

If no, proceed to Step 4.7.13: 8.3.3.6.13 Include variance analysis in Month End Reconciliation.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Coordinate to update Fixed Assets Master Data
steps.detail:
GFS Back Office R2R Team will inform Business / Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office through email about the master data errors, so that they can the request for changes to GFS Back Office DMT Team.

Reach out to GFS Back Office DMT team on the changes / updates required on the Master Data

The local team (Business / Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office) will need to send in the request via Email to maintain the corrections to the asset master data.

For changes to Master Data, the GFS Back Office DMT team will check that the form is filled correctly and accurately with all necessary information. They will then make the necessary changes in the asset’s Master Data in SAP and communicate back via email.

Once resolved, proceed again with Step 4.7.6: 8.3.3.6.6 Execute Depreciation at month-end (test run), to ensure that all updates to Fixed Assets Master Data have been reflected accordingly.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Include variance analysis in month-end reconciliation
steps.detail:
Include the depreciation analysis with comments and explanations into the formal reconciliation prepared each month, which compares fixed asset balances from SAP FI to the Fixed Asset register.

Include analysis into reconciliation document

Include summary of depreciation run and other supporting findings found in Step 4.7.10: 8.3.3.6.10: Investigate Variance.

Include the applicable variance explanation (illustrative example only).

Example of variance explanation

Once analysis has been included, proceed to Step 4.7.14: 8.3.3.6.14 Execute depreciation (production).

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Execute Depreciation (Production)
steps.detail:
Depreciation is allocated by cost centre defined in the Asset Master Record. The processer will run depreciation for all active fixed assets on a monthly basis, as per the Global Close Calendar. The depreciation key defines the method that will be used to calculate depreciation for the asset.

Depreciation areas are set up to calculate depreciation for different purposes such as Group book, Local GAAP or Tax depreciation.

The output of the depreciation process will be the depreciation postings in each of the relevant depreciation areas, by the amount calculated as defined by the depreciation key. This will result in an adjustment of the Net Book Value of the Fixed Assets. Note that Group book and Local GAAP depreciation are posted to the General Ledger (GL) at the same time upon running AFAB whilst Tax depreciation is displayed in the AA module for reporting purposes.

Note: Month end depreciation final run for NAM Hubs is performed with an automated background scheduled job on WD-3 (US time 22:00) on monthly basis. In case of any error in schedule job run then follow the steps in section A) Perform depreciation final run and B) View depreciation job in SAP.

Check status of scheduled test run for NAM

Use T-code AFBP to check the posting log of schedule run.

At parameter in the below SAP screen, input Company Code, Fiscal Year and Posting Period. Tick on “SchedMan Monitor” Schedule Manager and click on execute icon .

The following page displays all historical job logs. Double click on “Depreciation posting run” to update the status. The “green” status means posting run is complete without any error.

The next panel will appear as below. Click on “Additional Info”, to confirm the company code, and posting period. Click on back icon  to download the list of posting log.

On the next page, uncheck “SchedMan Monitor”, check on “List assets” then execute

The result of total depreciation posting will be displayed at the bottom of the report at column “Amount to be posted”. Take a copy of screenshot of the posting run result with time stamp as CPX011 control supporting.

Perform Final Depreciation Run

The below steps for Depreciation run are performed for all region except NAM. In case NAM scheduled job fails, then this step will need to be performed for NAM as well.

Access SAP and enter T-code AFAB. Press Enter.

Fill in the Company Code, Fiscal Year and current Posting Period. Make sure that “Test Run” has been unticked. Click on execute icon  to proceed:

Do NOT tick Test Run!

At the top left of the page, go to “Program”, then select “Execute in Background” (or F9).

A pop up “Background Print Parameters” will appear. Enter the Output Device as “local_en”.

Click on the green tick to continue.

Another pop up will appear for the user’s information only. Click on the green tick to continue.

Input when the final depreciation should be run. In this instance, final depreciation will be run immediately. So, click on “Immediate”, then click on Save  (or Ctrl+S).

At the bottom of the page, a message will appear which says, “Background job was scheduled for program RAPOST20000”.

View depreciation job in SAP

The below steps to view Depreciation job are performed for all region except NAM. In case NAM scheduled job fails, then this step will need to be performed for NAM as well.

From any page in SAP > click on “System” > then select “Own Jobs”.

Make sure the Job has the green status: “Finished”. If it is not finished yet, the status will state “Active”. In that case simply keep refreshing the page by clicking on the Refresh button (or “F8”).

This is a Finished Job. It will be highlighted in green.

Include Depreciation summary into analysis file

If the job has finished, this means that the Depreciation has been posted.

Proceed to select the job, then click Spool button.

Select the button, which will show the Spooled Final Depreciation Run.

Take a print screen of the spooled Final Depreciation Run, making sure to capture the heading of the spooled report as well as the depreciation totals at the bottom of the report.

Paste this into the Depreciation Analysis file in the “Dep Print Screen” Tab below the screenshot of the Depreciation Test Run done earlier.

Depreciation totals at bottom of report

Title of spooled report

The final depreciation run figures should be the same as the depreciation test run, but if for some reason there is a difference, the current month’s posted depreciation report can be extracted using the T-code AFAB as shown in Step 4.7.1: 8.6.6.3.1 Execute initial depreciation mid-month (test run) , and then input into the AFAB Tab (which is for the current month’s depreciation data).

Extract YTD depreciation amount from FA Sub-ledger

The YTD depreciation amount (by asset class) from the Fixed Assets subledger is taken from AR02 report. Go to T-code AR02.

Key in the company code and indicate report date as the last day of the month.

Change Sort Variant to “0007” and tick “… or group totals only”.

Click the Execute button (Or press F8).

Click Select Layout button , to change the Layout to “/CPX007_MEO”. Click on green tick to continue.

Click on “List”, then choose “Export” then click on “Spreadsheet” to export the AR02 report.

Below Screen will appear, click on green tick  as highlighted below.

Name the file and click Save.

Open the FA Movement Analysis Template (refer to Section 9: Appendices for location of file).

Copy the entire exported report into the FA Movement Analysis Template’s “AR02” Tab.

Take screenshots of the AR02 report in SAP and paste it into the “AR02” Tab under the AR02 table.

Perform final depreciation reconciliation with Financial Statement

In the Dep Analysis Tab Column J (YTD Depreciation), ensure correct SUMIF formula to calculate the asset class’ YTD depreciation amount from AR02 Column L.

Column J Formula: =SUMIF(AR02_RU10!C:C,'Dep Analysis_RU10'!A14,AR02_RU10!L:L)

Next, reconcile current month’s depreciation in Asset Register (purple table) with that in

P&L (green table).

Pull the Financial Statement using T-code: F.01.

Please update the following fields:

Company Code

Chart of Accounts “SCOA”

Financial Statement: “ZFSG”

For Reporting Year and Periods: input this year Period 1 to current month.

For Comparison Year and Periods: input last year’s Period 1 to 16.

Tick “ALV grid control” and use Layout: “/MEO-F.01”

Click the Execute button at the top of the page (or F8).

For YTD figures:

Reporting Year and Periods: this year, Period 1 to current month

The following pop up is for information only, so click the green tick (or Enter) to continue.

Export the resulting report by clicking on “List”, select “Export” click “Spreadsheet”.

The Save As pop up will appear. Save the report on the “Desktop” and name the file. Then click on “Save”.

Column G: this year’s YTD amount

Column H: last year’s YTD amount to Period 16

Column I: YTD movement

Copy the entire report and paste it into the Depreciation Analysis file in “F.01” Tab. Make sure the Account numbers (Column C) are converted from text to number.

The F.01 data will be used to populate the YTD Depreciation in the green P&L table in “Dep Analysis” Tab.

Ensure correct formula is present in Column K.

Column L’s values are linked to F.01 by using the formula to VLOOKUP from Column C to Column G in “F.01” Tab. This formula should not be adjusted.

Formula = IFERROR(VLOOKUP(K14,F.01!C:G,3,0),0)

The difference, Column M’s formula is found by adding Column L (P&L YTD Depreciation) with Column J (Asset Ledger YTD Depreciation Amount).

For GL Accounts which map to multiple Asset Classes, adjust the formula to add all the applicable Asset Classes’ “YTD Depreciation” value.

Column M should show zero difference, meaning that Depreciation in the Asset Register has been reconciled to the depreciation movements in the P&L statement.

Besides the screenshots of the test run and final run, there are two more print screens required in the Dep Print Screen Tab.

F.01 of the Accumulated Depreciation GLs in Balance Sheet

F.01 of the Depreciation Expense GLs in the Profit & Loss

Enter T-code F.01 and press Enter.

This time input the list of Accumulated Depreciation GLs into the GL account selection. Click Execute .

The total “Abs Diff” column should show the total depreciation posted in the month. Print Screen this and paste into the “Dep Print Screen” Tab.

Input T-code F.01 again.

This time input the list of Depreciation Expense GLs into the G/L account selection.

Press F8 or click on execute icon.

The total “Abs Diff” column should show the total depreciation posted in the month. Print Screen this and paste into the Dep Print Screen Tab.

The Depreciation Analysis section has been completed. Send the FA Movement and Analysis file to the reviewer. After the review is completed, save the file in the R2R working folder for the month.

Task # TASK NAME
8.4.2.4.1

Generate the open capital projects reports
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office

Open project reports are generated to keep track of open projects which might be subject for project closure (for example, percentage of completion based on actual amount and budget). Once generated, submit the report to Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office for review.

  1. Prepare Open Capital Project Report

The purpose of month end report for capital projects is to monitor the current open capital projects, budgeted amount against actual spend.

Log in to SAP system.

Enter T-code CN41N to extract open projects actual cost and budget.

Select the PS Info Profile “000000000001” in the pop-up screen and click the green tick .

Note: Project System Info Profile vary amongst different SAP instances. Please ensure you input according to the SAP instance that you are supporting.

At the parameter screen select Dynamic selections , double click on Company Code and input accordingly. Input multiple selection “E*” to include all projects in the project field.

Please note: If the selected country has some old projects code other than E, please include here as well.

Click F8 to Execute.

The report output is shown below:

Click on Extract icon as highlighted below and then on “MS Excel (xls)” to export the report into excel:

Select “Table” in the pop-up box and click on green tick to proceed as displayed below:

Click on “Microsoft Excel” and then on green tick to extract the report in excel:

py this data and place it in “Data ALL” tab in the monthly main file (Open project capital report). This is done to extract current open projects with budget and match the AUC balance against it.

The next step is to extract AUC asset balances and match AUC asset number against WBSE.

  1. Retrieve Asset List

Enter T-code AR02 (Asset History Sheet) or T-code is S_ALR_87011990 (Asset History Sheet) to extract AUC number and amounts. Fill in the parameters as per below instructions:

steps.title: Generate the open capital projects reports
steps.detail:
Open project reports are generated to keep track of open projects which might be subject for project closure (for example, percentage of completion based on actual amount and budget). Once generated, submit the report to Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office for review.

Prepare Open Capital Project Report

The purpose of month end report for capital projects is to monitor the current open capital projects, budgeted amount against actual spend.

Log in to SAP system.

Enter T-code CN41N to extract open projects actual cost and budget.

Select the PS Info Profile “000000000001” in the pop-up screen and click the green tick .

Note: Project System Info Profile vary amongst different SAP instances. Please ensure you input according to the SAP instance that you are supporting.

At the parameter screen select Dynamic selections , double click on Company Code and input accordingly. Input multiple selection “E*” to include all projects in the project field.

Please note: If the selected country has some old projects code other than E, please include here as well.

Click F8 to Execute.

The report output is shown below:

Click on Extract icon as highlighted below and then on “MS Excel (xls)” to export the report into excel:

Select “Table” in the pop-up box and click on green tick  to proceed as displayed below:

Click on “Microsoft Excel” and then on green tick to extract the report in excel:

py this data and place it in “Data ALL” tab in the monthly main file (Open project capital report). This is done to extract current open projects with budget and match the AUC balance against it.

The next step is to extract AUC asset balances and match AUC asset number against WBSE.

Retrieve Asset List

Enter T-code AR02 (Asset History Sheet) or T-code is S_ALR_87011990 (Asset History Sheet) to extract AUC number and amounts. Fill in the parameters as per below instructions:

Complete the following fields:

Company Code - Input Company code

Asset class - range from 9000 to 9599 (please refer the AUC asset classes as per your respective SAP instances)

Report Date - Current month-end

Depreciation Area - “20” (“Cost-acc”) (please refer Local Book for respective SAP instances)

Sort variant: Please select Sort Variant with WBSE Reference

Choose “List assets”.

Click Select Layout button  to change the Layout to “/MEO”, which will display a summary of asset movement during the year by asset class.

Choose Layout - “/MEO” as mentioned above and click on green tick.

Press F8 to Execute or click on  icon and it will generate the report with asset class as given below:

Click “List”, choose “Export” and then click on “Spreadsheet” to extract the AR02 report in excel:

Name the file and click on “Save”.

The excel report will appear as below and will be used in the subsequent step C) Extract report for AUC with WBSE reference to match against WBSE.

Extract report for AUC with WBSE reference

Enter T-code S_ALR_87012058 (List of Origins of Asset Charges) to extract AUC assets with WBSE number.

Fill in the below details and click on execute icon :

Asset number: Copy all the AUC asset numbers from AR02 list and paste  the list at asset number in SAP

Report date: Current month-end date

Depreciation Area: Please refer local books for respective SAP instances.

Sort Variant: Please select Sort Variant with WBSE Reference

The screen will appear as below:

The report will appear as below. Click on Systems at menu bar > List > Save > Local File to extract the report in excel. Follow the below steps to save the extracted excel file:

Click on List

Select Save

Local file

Text with Tabs

Enter the File Name

Click on Generate

Using the report from S_ALR_87012058, VLOOKUP the WBSE element number at Column I to the AR02 report (Column D) with AUC asset numbers.

Use the formula in D2 in AR02 report “=VLOOKUP(A2,[Report] S_ALR_87012058_SE10!A:I,9,0)”

Subsequently, create another column (Column C) in AR02 report to capture the project definition (e.g. E.012641.05.01 to E.012641). Use the formula “=left(D2,8)”

The screen will appear as below:

The next step is to create a Pivot by following the steps as given below:

Select the table range for which you want to create a pivot in the pop-up box and click “OK”: -

A pivot table will be created on the same tab below the table. Select the rows and values for the pivot table as given below:

Filter level “00” in Column B in CN41N report. Insert a VLOOKUP formula:

=VLOOKUP(D116,’Extraction from AR02’!$A$3931:$B$4895,2,0) to copy the AUC balances from AR02 report pivot table with project ID at Column D.

Filter Level “00”

Ensure that the AUV balance tie with AR02

VLOOKUP AUC balances from AR02 report

Use the below report for VLOOKUP formulas in above sheet:

VLOOKUP AUC balances from AR02 report

The final Open Project Report with “Actual Cost” and “Budget” appears as below:

To support CAPEX 3 reporting, T-code CN41N displays cumulative authorised budget of all projects against the project’s life.

To match sub-ledger AR02 AUC balance with General Ledger, enter T-code F.01.

Fill in the below fields:

Chart of Accounts: SCOA

G/L Account: Input the G/L accounts for which AUC balance is to be verified by clicking on the highlighted icon, inputting the AUC G/L Numbers and then click on execute icon

Reporting Year: Current Year

Click on icon against G/L account to enter more than one G/L account.

Enter the GL numbers to be used as shown below:

Once all the details are entered, press F8 or click execute icon  to proceed.

Below screen shows the output:

Verify the AUC balance in F.01 from AR02 and prepare a working as shown below keeping the screenshots of balances verified as shown below:

AR02 excel extract is given below to verify the balance:

The reason for balance mismatch, if any, would be due to manual posting to AUC GL 12100901, supporting will need to be provided in the report at Manual Posting” tab.

Save a copy of the Open Capital Project Report by pasting the data as values in the report and share the file with GFS Middle Office and respective project managers.

steps.title: Review and determine capital projects for closure
steps.detail:
Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office performs a review of the open capital projects report submitted by GFS Back Office R2R to identify projects for closure. A review of open projects or assets in the course of construction should be completed to confirm assets brought into use. This will also serve as a reminder for Project Managers to close their respective capital projects.

Determine capital projects for closure

Review the received report focusing on “% Compl.” Field. Communicate with the respective Project Managers on whether the project with 90% completion rate is ready for closure and capitalisation. Business will make a decision on closing based on their knowledge of the status of the project.

The report will appear as below with “% completion” in Column P:

steps.title: Validate and confirm capital projects for closure
steps.detail:
Submit the open capital projects report to the Business for review. The Business validates and confirms capital projects for closure based on their knowledge of the status of the project.

steps.title: Initiate project Capitalisation and/or close
steps.detail:
The Business makes the decision to initiate the project closure once Business and Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office confirm and validate all expenses.

steps.title: Review of capital project expenditure
steps.detail:
Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office reviews the capital project expenditure before proceeding to the final settlement run. Capital expenditures are reviewed against the budget assigned to the project.

Receive Assets Master Data Maintenance Template

The project manager or Business partner shares the Assets Master Data Maintenance Template via email.

Check the Assets Master Data Maintenance Template

Ensure all fields in “Assets Master Data Maintenance Template” Tab “Assets Master Data Maint Tmplte” in red / marked with an asterisk are completed as per screenshots below:

Refer “Instructions” tab in the template for details.

Fill out the “Tax useful life” field based on local taxation ruling or another authorised source if applicable.

Compare Capital expenditures against the budget

In order to get the value of the asset (in local currency), go to SAP and key in T-code “S_ALR_87013558”.

Click on Dynamic selection icon  then under “Org. units definition”. Input Company code and Controlling Area or click on to input details. Enter “E*” in “Project field” for all capital projects. Click on “execute” icon.

The report appears as below. Convert the report to local currency by clicking on “Currency selection” .

Current selection

Input local currency in “Currency” column and select “Default for drilldown reporting” in “Translation Key” column from the drop-down options, then click on “Execute”  icon.

steps.detail:
After ensuring all details are correct, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office requests GDO Back Office DMT for creation of asset shell with the updated templates.

Send a request for asset shell creation

Once the Assets Master Data Maintenance Template is complete, send the completed template for approval to the GFS Middle Office team lead. A sample email approval request is shown below:

A sample email approval is shown below:

Receive and validate request to create a new capital asset

A.1) Receive a request for new capital asset creation

GDO Back Office DMT accesses the Assets Master Data Maintenance Template through the mailbox. In case of Hubs, NPC template will be used instead of Assets Master Data Maintenance Template.

Note: Refer to the hubs-specific SOP for details. Please refer appendices for link.

steps.title: Perform final settlement (WBSE to AUC)
steps.detail:
GFS Back Office R2R checks the asset under construction identified to be put into operations. Then performs the settlement process from WBSE to AUC.

Please note: The AUC settlement can be both single and mass settlement. Refer step A) Single settlement and B) Mass settlement for details.

Single settlement

A.1) Test run for single settlement

Enter T-code CJ88 and press Enter.

Key in the Project Number and execute in the present period. Execute Test Run to check for any errors.

The Settlement will show a page like below.

A.2) Run actual single settlement

After ensuring settlement can run correctly without error, go back to the previous page (Press F3).

Untick Test Run and proceed to Execute.

The result after the actual run will be as follows:

A.3) Check settlement run results

CJ88 will move costs from WBSE to AUC by triggering the following entry:

Debit AUC GL Asset Under Construction/AICC

Credit 99101090 Capital project settlement

After settlement, check that 99101090 and 99100010 combinations net off to zero. This can be examined via CJI3 or F.01.

Option 1: CJI3 - Display WBSE actual costs by line item

Option 2: F.01 - Display Financial Statement

A.4) Check settlement values posts to GL

Also, check that the settlement is posted into the correct AUC GL. This can be examined via FBL3N. Enter T-code FBL3N in SAP:

Key in Company Code

Key in G/L account: 99100010 and 99101090

Key in all items posting date: Current month.

Check “Offset.acct” column to ensure the settlement has posted into AUC GL - 12XXXXXX.

Mass settlement

B.1) Test run for mass settlement

Enter T-code CJ8G in SAP and press Enter:

Below screen will appear. Enter Controlling Area:

Key in the Settlement and posting period, fiscal year and choose processing type “automatic type”. Please ensure “Test run”, “Detail list” & “Check. Trans data” should be ticked in Processing Options box. Then click the pencil icon to check the variant parameter.

For single project selection and input specific WBS element under “Select Single Values”.

Further on same screen, click on “Select Ranges” tab and key in “00000 to 29999” and click execute  button.

Below screen will appear, now click on dynamic icon on the left of the screen as highlighted below and input Project number:

Key in company code which needs to be excluded, if any.

Note: If extracting the data for UK only, exclude the data for UK40,UK46 and UK47 as these company codes are for UK MEDI. To exclude multiple company codes, click on the right arrow icon in above screen and enter the company codes in “Exclude Single Values tab”. Eg. For UK key in UK40,UK46 and UK47 and click on execute  icon.

Click F8 to run T-code CJ8G in background:

Key in “LOCL Generic Frontend Printing” in the output device icon.

Key in Page 1 until 10000000 in page icon.

Choose “Immediately” in Print time drop-down.

Then click the green tick. Sap will run in background.

Go to SAP T-code SM37.

Check the status as “Finished” means the file is finished and executed. Double click the spool icon.

After clicking on the Spool icon in above screen, below screen will pop up ,double click on ABAP list:

Key in the settings from “page 1 to 100000” in the pop-up box which comes on clicking on “Settings”.

Click on the green tick in below screen:

File will be executed in excel, if there is no error, run CJ8G without ticking the test run. If there is any error, please rectify them and run CJ8G without ticking the test run.

If there is no error, screen will show as below. (Please note the project number E.009260 shown here is for illustrative purposes only. It doesn’t match with the above template).

If there is an error, screen will appear as below:

Examples of errors are shared below:

Follow the steps below to rectify if the error is about the settlement rule. Here we are referring to WBS Element E.009851.01.04.10 as an example.

To resolve error of Settlement rule, please enter T-code CJ02 in SAP:

Below screen will pop up, key in WBS element and press Enter:

Fill in the below fields:

In Cat field key in: WBS,

In “%” field key in: “100”,

In Settlement type field key in “FUL”

Now click on “Ctrl+S”.

Then run back again in CJ88, WBS will be executed and check in CJI3 again amount will be zero. That means the unsettled amount will be fully settled.

Note: In case the error pertains to one WBS, use SAP T-code CJ88 to settle errors. In other cases where errors occur in more than one WBS, use T-code CJ8G.

B.2) Run actual mass settlement

After rectifying all the errors, re-run CJ8G again and if the report is executed successfully with no errors, un-tick the test run and run back again the CJ8G for an actual production run.

Enter T-code CJ8G in SAP and press Enter:

Below screen appears when settlement run without error:

If error occurs, follow the steps mentioned in Step 4.7.9: 8.4.2.2.9 Perform monthly settlement clearing (WBSE to AUC) to run CJ8G to resolve errors.

steps.detail:

Receive and validate request to capitalise asset

Validate the AUC Settlement template received in email. Please find below the AUC template for reference.
