steps.title: Monitor and collect project transactions
steps.detail:
Business has the responsibility to monitor and collect project transactions such as goods / service receipt, salary expenses, material movements, time expenses and T&E expenses.

The following types of transactions can be posted to the project:

Goods / services procured: Please proceed to the process 4.3.3.4 Perform Indirect Materials Purchase (i-Buy) and then to 4.3.3.6 Perform goods or service receipt

Salary expenses: Please proceed to the process 8.3.2.10 Post payroll

Material movements: Please proceed to step 4.7.2: 8.4.2.2.2 Post material movements

Time expenses: Please proceed to step 4.7.3: 8.4.2.2.3 Post time expenses

T&E expenses: Please proceed to step 4.7.4: 8.4.2.2.4 Post T&E expenses

Clinical trial accruals: Please proceed to the process 8.6.1.23 Prepare and post clinical trial accruals

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Post material movements
steps.detail:
Direct materials used for project related activities must be monitored and recorded to the specific project. For example, for R&D projects, materials could be issued as part of R&D work.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Post time expenses
steps.detail:
Time expenses related to the execution of project are recorded in Cross Application Time Sheet (CATS) in UK and Sweden only and through normal payroll in other regions.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Post T&E expenses
steps.detail:
T&E expenses linked to projects must be recorded to underlying project.

(Note: T&E expenses come via concur and can be posted as long as the postings come with the WBSE code)

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Review expenses posted to the project
steps.detail:
Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office reviews and validates the expenses for completeness, accuracy and propriety, if applicable, to ensure all project expenditures are captured:

Salary expenses related to the execution of project

Time expenses recorded

Material costs and quantity

T&E report is validated and analysed to determine completeness, accuracy and propriety of expenses

After the review and validation, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office sends review request to the project managers. The Project Manager reviews to ensure that all expenses posted to the project are valid. Costs that are not directly associated with the project should not be posted to the project code. For capital projects, all expenses will be capitalised monthly and whenever the asset is ready to be brought into service.

Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office must determine if adjustments will be required in the recorded project related transactions.

Please ensure to perform control CPX004 as per the FCAS framework for the respective unit.

Review expenses posted to the project

Pre-month end closing activities may identify project related costs that are incorrectly posted to site costs. This should be picked up during site cost review performed in Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office and is later queried with the local site finance team or capital projects team. Sample query:

Sample query is shown below (PO 4800059428):

Sample query is shown below (PO 4800059823):

Embedded finance and the Project Manager review these queries and confirm back to GFS Middle Office, if any adjustment is required.

Representative Offices

Representative offices located in MEA and Europe will need to follow below steps to record Fixed Asset posting in UK or Sweden Hubs book.

Request a capital project via CAS, please proceed to 8.4.1.3 Review and approve capital projects for details.

Upon invoice on purchase of Fixed Asset posted, a journal entry will need to be passed in Hubs book. Please proceed to Step 4.7.6: 8.4.2.2.6 Prepare manual adjustments.

For Sweden, journal entry will need to be posted with GL 99100010 with WBSE and subsequently settle into AUC via 99101090 (For UK - Accounts are 70770150 and 70770160 respectively)

Subsequent to settlement, Middle Office Finance will need to send in Notice of Project Closure Template (NPC) to capitalise the Fixed Asset in UK or Sweden Hubs book. Please proceed to Step 4.7.6: 8.4.2.4 Close and capitalise projects for details.

Possible outcomes:

In case adjustment is required, then proceed to Step 4.7.6: 8.4.2.2.6 Prepare manual adjustments

In case adjustment is not required, and

WBSE is not statistical, then proceed to Step 4.7.7: 8.4.2.2.7 Perform monthly settlement clearing (WBSE to AUC)

WBSE is statistical, then go proceed Step 4.7.8: 8.4.2.2.8 Prepare month-end reports

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Prepare manual adjustments
steps.detail:
If adjustment is required, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office prepare the related manual journal templates for processing and raise them in their workflow tool.

Prepare manual adjustments

The adjustment for costs can be various. Among the examples (list is not exhaustive) are:

Accruing capital costs

Adjusting from site costs to AUC cost line

Reclassifying costs from one project to another

Recharging payroll costs to the project where individuals are part / full-time on a project

Please proceed to 8.3.2.2 Process Manual Journal Entries for further details on how the journal entry is submitted, approved and posted.

Once the adjustment review is complete, please proceed to step 4.7.7:8.4.2.2.7 Perform monthly settlement clearing (WBSE to AUC) for a non-statistical WBSE. For a statistical WBSE, please proceed to step 4.7.8:8.4.2.2.8 Prepare month-end reports.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Perform monthly settlement clearing (WBSE to AUC)
steps.detail:
Note: This step is not applicable to Brazil as it will continue to follow the current process until the configuration activities are completed by SAP IT team.

Once all project related transactions are raised, validated and posted, GFS Back Office R2R (Fixed Assets) proceeds with the monthly settlement clearing for capital project WBSE to transfer charges against WBSE to the AUC accounts. This occurs via a settlement rule created against the WBSE in the project structure. This is an important control point as costs on all capital projects are zeroed at month-end.

Prior to the fixed asset module closing at each month end, run T-code CJ88 (Individual WBS Settlement) / CJ8G (Mass month end WBS settlement) to settle (transfer) WBSE element costs into the corresponding AUC.

Please note that for NAM, due to large WBSE transaction volumes to AUC, a settlement background job is scheduled on daily basis at 23:00 US time with additional manual settlement during month-end.

Please find below process steps to run CJ88 for individual WBS settlement and CJ8G for mass month-end settlement.

Individual WBS settlement

Log in to SAP system.

A.1) Test run monthly settlement

To run settlement of actual WBSE costs enter T-code CJ88 and press Enter.

Key in WBS Element Number and execute in the present period.

Execute  as Test Run to check for any error.

The Settlement screen will appear as below.

Click on detail list icon on the left corner to see the settled cost for AUC and asset number.

Ensure processing is complete without any errors and there is settlement executed, which reflects in the above screenshot as highlighted.

After clicking on the detail list, the screen will appear as below:

In case the processing remains incomplete due to errors, a screen like below will appear. Double click on the error message to display the error messages.

Below is an indicative list of errors commonly observed in CJ88 (list is not exhaustive) and the actions to be taken to resolve them:

Error Type

Reason

Action

Yellow

There are remaining balances in AUC

No action is needed. This error will reflect in partial completion of Capitalisation. It can be processed as usual.

Red

The settlement amount exceeds the AUC Balances

Check the AUC amount in CJI3 with the capitalisation amount. If there is a variance, check the errors and rectify the same.

Re-run the processing until all errors are resolved and processing is successful.

A.2) Run actual monthly settlement

After ensuring the settlement runs correctly without errors, go back to the previous page (Press F3). This time untick Test Run and proceed to Execute .

The result after the actual run will be as follows:

A.3) Check settlement run results

CJ88 will move costs from WBSE to AUC by triggering the following entry:

Debit AUC GL Asset Under Construction / AICC / AUC

Credit Capital project settlement

After settlement, check that 99101090 and 99100010 combination nets off to zero. This can be examined via CJI3 or F.01

Note: Instead of the above GLs, ICON UK2 uses group of GLs / 70390120.

Option 1: CJI3 - Display the WBSE actual costs by line items.

For steps to use CJI3, refer to Step 8.4.2.2.8: 4.7.8 Prepare month end reports.

Note: This option is not applicable for UK, as UK has more than 20 cost elements where other posting without WBSE is possible, hence F.01 will not net off to zero.

Also, check that settlement is posted into correct AUC GL. This can be examined via T-code FBL3N displaying G/L Account Line Items:

TASK NAME

steps.title: Prepare month-end reports
steps.detail:
Note: This step is not applicable to Brazil as it will continue to follow the current process until the configuration activities are completed by SAP IT Team.

Open project reports are generated to keep track of open projects which might be subject for project closure. Submit these reports to Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office for review.

Prepare month-end report file for capital projects

The purpose of month - end report for capital projects is to monitor the current open capital projects, budgeted amount against actual spend.

Please note that below steps are not applicable for NAM, there is a customised report “ZRF11N - Capital Investment Report” used as a month-end report.

Log in to SAP system.

Enter T-code CN41N to extract open projects actual cost and budget.

Below screen will be displayed:

Select the PS Info Profile in the screen which appears and click the “Green tick”

At the Parameter Screen select Dynamic selections, double click on Company Code and input accordingly.

At Project field, input multiple selection: E* to include all projects.

Please note: For countries with some old project codes other than E, details are given below:

For UK, some old projects start with “C” and numerical 5 digits project numbers.

For Sweden, some old projects start with “C” and “S”, and

For NAM, old projects start with “C”

Click F8 or press  to Execute.

Report output is shown below:

Click on Extract and then on “MS Excel (xls)” to export the report into excel:

Select “Table” in the pop-up box and click on green tick  to proceed as displayed below:

Click on “Microsoft Excel” and then on green tick to extract the report in excel:

Copy this data and place it in “Data ALL” tab in the monthly main file.

Extract AUC asset balances and match AUC asset number against WBSE

The next step is to extract AUC asset balances and match AUC asset number against WBSE

Enter T-code AR02 (Asset History Sheet) or T-code is S_ALR_87011990 (Asset History Sheet) to extract AUC number and amounts. Fill in the Parameter using below:

Company code: Enter relevant company code

Asset class: Enter your company code AUC asset classes

Report date: Current month-end

Depreciation Area: 20 (please refer Local Book for respective SAP instances)

Sort variant: Please select Sort Variant with WBSE Reference.

If sort variant with WBSE is not available in your SAP instance, please run t-code S_ALR_87012058 (List of Origins of Asset Charges) to retrieve AUC with WBSE reference. Refer to Step 4.7.8: 8.4.2.2.8 Prepare month-end reports

Below is a screenshot sample of AR02 parameter for Sweden with sort variant: 0007 without WBSE.

Click Select Layout button  to change the Layout to “/MEO”, which will display a summary of asset movement during the year by asset class.

Choose Layout - “/MEO” as mentioned above and click on green tick.

Press F8 to Execute and it will generate the report with asset class.

It will be displayed as below and export it in excel.

To export in excel click  icon.

Choose the option “Text with Tabs” and click the green tick button .

Select the location to save the file.

Change the save as type from “txt” to “xls” and hit Save button:

Below is the data in Excel:

Extract the report for AUC with WBSE reference

Enter T-code S_ALR_87012058 (List of Origins of Asset Charges) to extract AUC assets with WBSE number.

Copy all the AUC assets from AR02 List (as shown below) and paste  the list in asset number field in SAP.

Fill in the below details:

Asset number: copy all the AUC assets from AR02 List and paste values  the list at asset number in SAP by clicking on Multiple selection icon. Click green tick button  to save the data.

Report date: current month-end

Depreciation Area: (please refer Local Book for respective SAP instances)

Sort Variant: 0003

Press F8 or click Execute Button

Extract the report in excel: Upon extracted report displayed, click at System at menu bar > List > Save > Local File. Then select the designated folder to save the file.

Using the report from S_ALR_87012058, VLOOKUP the WBSE element number at Column I to the AR02 report’s (Column D) with AUC asset numbers.

Use the formula in O6 in AR02 report “=VLOOKUP(B6,[Report] S_ALR_87012058_SE10!A:M,10,0)”

(e.g. E.012641.05.01 to E.012641)

Going back to CN41N report, refer Step 8.4.2.2.8:4.6.8 A) Prepare month-end reports, filter only level “00” and VLOOKUP the AUC balances from AR02 report with project ID.

Create a new column (Column O) in AR02 report to capture the project definition (e.g. E.012641.05.01 to E.012641). Use the formula “=VLOOKUP(O6,[Report] AR02!A:M,12,0)”

## Source file: Preclose Analysis.docx

- Path: `Tower Subprocesses/FP&A Commercial/Preclose Analysis.docx`
- Format: DOCX

**Transcript 4 — Pre-close Analysis**

**1. Purpose and Business Objective**

The Pre-close Analysis process performs **month-end pre-close review** of current financial performance and estimates the expected month-end position **before formal close is completed**. It identifies significant variances, unusual transactions, and potential risks or opportunities early, ensuring key issues are investigated and communicated in a timely manner while supporting a smoother and more accurate close.

The output enables management and finance teams to **assess whether the business is tracking in line with expectations** and to take pre-close action where needed. It supports decisions on variance investigation, issue escalation, accrual or adjustment review, forecast updates, and communication of expected results to stakeholders.

When delayed or inaccurate, **key financial issues may not be identified early enough** for proper review or action before close. This can lead to inaccurate reporting, delayed escalation, weaker decision-making, close-process inefficiencies, reduced confidence in reported numbers, and missed financial risks or opportunities.

**2. Trigger and Timing**

The process runs monthly and is triggered by month-end close activity. It typically begins at **WD-4**, once payroll booking is complete, with PO accruals posted at **WD-3**. The deadline for completion is **WD-1 or WD1**, depending on the market, and the total duration is around **four to five working days**. The timeline does not change during budget or forecast cycles.

**3. Inputs and Data Sources**

Two primary inputs are required: **month-end closing data** (sales, COGS, cost data) from **SAP and CMR**; and **planning cycle data** from **CMR**.

Data quality is inconsistent — **booked data in SAP can be inaccurate due to incorrect source inputs**. Validation occurs during closing, when analysts review SAP data to ensure alignment with accounting standards.

**4. Stakeholders and Responsibilities**

Input is drawn from **SAP and CMR**, with execution performed by **FP&A**. Reviewers and challengers include **FP&A, the Controller, and the CFO**, with **CFO sign-off** required. Final recipients are the **CFO and CP**.

The process depends on **financial functions that book data into SAP** and on **controllers who post journal accruals**. **Delays occur when requested correction journals are not booked in time**.

**5. Tools and Methods**

The process uses the **Preclose File, SAP, and CMR data** to present the latest SAP data in P&L or department format and compare against planning cycles. Automation level is **semi-automated**. The Excel workbook contains **multiple tabs, uses macros/VBA, and is shared simultaneously**.

**6. Step-by-Step Process Flow**

The process begins in **Step 1** with FP&A downloading actual SAP details and refreshing planning numbers into the Preclose file. In **Step 2**, FP&A reviews and analyses revenue and cost by comparing actuals against planning and deep-diving into SAP details. **Step 3** involves identifying variances, preparing commentary, or requesting corrections for inaccurate journal postings. **Step 4** repeats Steps 1 to 3 as needed until numbers are finalised for closing.

In **Step 5**, FP&A prepares commentary on variances and readies the pre-close presentation for CBP and CFO review. **Step 6** captures CFO comments and applies required changes. Finally, **Step 7** ensures the final Preclose file numbers align to CMR.

A **key decision point** is that Preclose analysis is highly dependent on the quality of SAP booked data — high inaccuracy increases the correction burden and delays commentary output. Additionally, **SAP data is extracted multiple times daily during pre-close** to ensure corrections are captured and the latest data is used.

**7. Output and Deliverable Structure**

The final output is the **Preclose File**, delivered as an **Excel file**. Granularity spans **market/country, brand/product, P&L line, and cost centre**. Templates are **mostly standardised with minor variations**, and outputs are stored on **SharePoint and Box**.

**8. Validation, Controls, and Approval**

Two manual validation checks are performed: a **full P&L line and cost centre level check**, and a **total check against extracted actuals and CMR**. A formal approval gate exists, with the **CFO signing off**. The process typically requires **four or more revision cycles**. When errors are found post-submission, corrections are applied based on CFO comments, with typically one to two working days of correction runway available. There are **no SOX-relevant or audit-relevant controls** embedded in this task.

**9. Dependencies and Interconnections**

Detail journal booking in SAP must be complete or available at **WD-3** before this task can begin. The output feeds into the **Preclose Review with the CFO**. A one to two day delay eliminates the Preclose review window and prevents any month-end number amendments. Uncaught errors typically surface in **downstream revenue or cost reporting** or in the Preclose file itself.

**10. Pain Points, Risks, and Improvement Opportunities**

Three pain points dominate. First, **inaccurate bookings of raw data** require multiple corrections and scrutiny before real analysis can occur. Second, **delayed replies from budget owners** on variance queries slow the process. Third, **SAP data changes frequently**, requiring close monitoring to ensure alignment with month-end expectations.

Pain points fall across **data quality, tight timelines, and frequent rework loops**. The primary risk is that if this task is not done correctly, **financial numbers reported for the month will be inaccurate**, potentially leading to wrong business decisions.

The primary improvement opportunity is to establish a **standard Preclose review online platform across all markets**. FCT is currently used, but it sources from CMR, which has a data capture lag compared to SAP.
